title: OpenChamber extensions
excerpt: Three panels for the OpenChamber rail to manage OpenCode agents, skills, and MCP servers from the interface, without leaving the browser.
challenge: Managing OpenCode agents, skills, and MCP servers requires editing files by hand, remembering their keys, and switching context between terminal and editor. There is no centralized view or quick switch to turn each one on or off.
solution:
Three OpenChamber extensions, each a panel on the rail. Each edits the plain files OpenCode already reads. The files stay where they are and the format does not change.

Agents panel
List, turn on, turn off, edit, and create OpenCode agents. Agents remain plain markdown files.
[https://github.com/N4N1T0/openchamber-agents](https://github.com/N4N1T0/openchamber-agents)

Global lists ~/.config/opencode/agents and the agent/ folder. Project lists .opencode/agents of the open project. Each row shows name, mode, description, model.

A switch per row turns an agent off or on. Off writes disable: true into the frontmatter; on removes the key. Change is immediate, reverts only if the write fails.

Click a row to edit: name (new agents), description, mode, model, temperature, instructions, tool permissions. Tool permissions: default value, every built-in and OpenChamber tool, one row per MCP server from your global opencode.json, and patterns under any tool. Inherit, Allow, Ask, Deny. Rules not listed (bash, write) stay written.

New creates an agent after checking the name and that the file does not exist. Delete takes two clicks. Search filters by name, description, model.

Changes land in new sessions; a running session keeps its agent.

Built-in agents (build, plan, general, explore) are not files, not listed. Neither are agents declared in opencode.json. This panel edits only markdown agent files. Shadow a built-in by creating one with the same name.

VS Code and the phone do not load extensions.

Skills panel
Hide skills from the model, show them again, edit, and create new ones. Skills remain SKILL.md files.
[https://github.com/N4N1T0/openchamber-skills](https://github.com/N4N1T0/openchamber-skills)

Global lists ~/.config/opencode/skills, ~/.claude/skills and ~/.agents/skills. Project lists .opencode/skills, .claude/skills and .agents/skills of the open project. Row: name, description, path. Badge if from a compatibility folder.

Switch hides or shows a skill. Off writes disable-model-invocation: true; on removes it. Change is immediate.

A hidden row appears dimmed with Off. It only means the model does not offer it; it stays registered and loadable with @id.

Click to edit ID (new skills), display name, description, instructions body. Save applies. The hide switch stays as is.

Checks as you type: no description (error); over 500 characters (warning); overridden by higher-precedence folder (warning); no instructions (warning); no frontmatter (warning); duplicate ID (error); description without when-to-use (warning); hidden with trigger description (info); ID not kebab-case (info); name differs from ID (info); hidden by switch or metadata (info).

New creates a skill: folder with SKILL.md or a single <id>.md file, and its folder. Folder list offers OpenCode's own, plus .claude and .agents only when they exist. Checks the ID and that nothing is there.

Delete takes two clicks; a folder skill removes the folder with scripts and references. Search filters by name, ID, description.

Changes land in new sessions; a running session keeps its skills.

Built-in OpenCode skills are not files, not listed. Skills in the skills[] array of opencode.json, HTTP catalogs, and hiding permissions are not visible. The switch writes disable-model-invocation. metadata with opencode/autoinvoke: false wins; the panel reports it and leaves both.

MCP panel
See which MCP servers OpenCode has configured, which are on, inspect full configuration, remove them. Servers stay in opencode.json.
[https://github.com/N4N1T0/openchamber-mcps](https://github.com/N4N1T0/openchamber-mcps)

Global lists ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json and .jsonc. Project needs an open project and lists opencode.json(c) and .opencode/opencode.json(c). Row: name, local/remote, URL or command, file and line.

A switch keeps a server from connecting or lets it connect. Off writes "disabled": true; on removes the key. Change is immediate.

The entry stays as is. An off server remains configured with URL, headers, sign-in. OpenCode picks up the change without restart; a running session keeps its tools.

Click a row for detail: type, URL or command, working folder, sign-in, tool names, Code Mode, protocol, pooling, timeouts, switch key, headers and environment, every notice, entry exactly as written.

Headers and environment values that look like credentials are masked, with Reveal. {env:NAME} is never masked.

Notices:
- no usable type: error
- remote without absolute http(s) url: error
- local without command: error
- enabled under mcp.servers: warning (V2 ignores it; only disabled turns off)
- V1 placement mcp.<name>: warning (still loaded, switched by enabled)
- credential written in file: warning
- credential over plain http://: warning
- $VAR in header or environment: warning (use {env:VAR})
- oauth: false with no credential: warning
- pool: true on local without cwd: warning
- V1 timeout: 5000: warning (V2 wants { startup, catalog, execution })
- another file same name: warning (replaces whole entry)
- two names one tool prefix: warning (normalizes)
- header credential with OAuth on: info (oauth: false stops sign-in)
- codemode: false: info (every tool takes context per session)
- pool: true with protocol legacy: info (only 2026-07-28 shared)
- keys OpenCode does not define: info (kept, ignored)
- name changes to tool name: info (says what tools are called)
- disabled: false: info (default; offers to remove)
- server off: info (configured, not connected)

A notice one key too many (enabled where it does nothing, disabled: false) carries the remove button.

Delete takes two clicks; removes that entry from that file, leaves everything else. Search filters by name, URL, command. Reload re-reads files.

No local service, no network origin. Only reads and writes those config files.

Installation
Install each extension separately. In OpenChamber, Settings > Extensions, paste the repository URL. Approve file access. Deleting requires a local service in agents and skills; until approved, delete is unavailable and the rest works.

Skills and MCPs are released as tags. Add one to the install URL to stay on that version: …/openchamber-skills#v1.0.0.

What they do not do
- they do not list built-in OpenCode agents or skills (not files)
- they do not list agents or skills declared inside opencode.json
- the MCP panel shows configuration, not connection state. It cannot say whether a server is reachable, whether sign-in expired, or which tools it offers; that needs a live OpenCode: opencode mcp list or /mcps
- switching off is not disconnecting: config change; a running session keeps its tools
- adding a server is not in the panel: use opencode mcp add
- deleting an entry leaves OAuth credentials stored; opencode mcp logout <name> removes them
- permissions are not edited here: permissions can hide or deny tools without touching config; this panel edits mcp, not permissions
- VS Code and the phone do not load extensions

Development
Each repository uses Bun. Built .js files are committed; CI fails if they differ from sources. Rebuild and commit after every source change.
